title: human PBMCs from recovered adolescents_003
extract_protocol_ch1: Whole blood was collected in a tube containing ethylene diamine tetraacetic acid (EDTA). PBMCs were isolated by Ficoll-Hypaque density gradient centrifugation with LymphoprepTM solution (AXIS-SHIELD Poc AS, Oslo, Norway) according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. The mononuclear cell layer was carefully transferred to a new 15 mL conical tube and washed twice with RPMI 1640 medium (Hyclone, Logan, UT, USA) by centrifuging at 486 × g for 10 min at room temperature. PBMCs were resuspended in RPMI 1640 culture medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Millipore, Danvers, MA, USA), 100 units/mL penicillin, and 100 μg/mL streptomycin (GIBCO, Grand Island, NY, USA).

Single cell RNA (sc-RNA) libraries of PBMCs were prepared according to the guideline from the Chromium Single Cell 5' v3 chemistry (10x Genomics, Cat No. 120237) based on the Drop-seq methodology. The libraries were sequenced using Illumina nova S6000 device by Genergy Biotechnology (Shanghai, China).
data_processing: scRNA sequencing reads were subjected to quality control based on FastQC software v0.11.9 (https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/). Then, we used Cell Ranger software (version 3.1.0) to process, align, and summarize sequencing data. Demultiplex FASTQ reads were aligned to the human genome reference (GRCh38-3.0.0). Reads with low base-calling quality scores and assigned cell barcodes were filtered. Unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts of each transcript were quantified. UMI matrix was converted to Seurat objects by the R package Seurat v3. Further analysis was performed by R package. Raw UMI count matrices were filtered to remove the genes expressed in fewer than three cells and the cells with either fewer than 200 genes, or more than 6000 genes, or high percentages of mitochondrial genes (more than 15%). To account for the differences in sequencing depth across the cells, UMI count was then normalized by a global-scaling method, converted with a scaling factor (10,000 by the default) and log-transformed with the LogNormalize function in Seurat for downstream analysis.
